natural_body: 40% discounts raise acquisition and revenue but hurt retention and renewals.

first.rationale: With only one experiment slot, the two internally-controllable metrics in decline (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) are more directly addressable and carry durable prior evidence (memory_86 on shortened onboarding, memory_31 on signup simplification) than a reactive price-matching move. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor pressure but the archived record flags it as harming retention despite short-term acquisition/revenue gains, which conflicts with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue; verifying it before ruling it out is prudent given the competitive urgency. Verifying memory_86 confirms the onboarding-shortening evidence base before committing the single weekly slot to it. Choosing simplify_onboarding directly targets the onboarding completion decline, has strong durable support, and avoids the retention risk flagged for discount-driven acquisition, while a standard (not broad) rollout preserves ability to reassess given three simultaneous pressures.
